verses.1: The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son is the mother’s disgrace.
verses.2: Wrongdoing will not save the wicked, but righteousness rescues from death.
verses.3: The Lord will not let the soul of the righteous go hungry, but the desires of the wicked will be thwarted.
verses.4: A hardworking hand is a head of gold, but lazy hands bring poverty.
verses.5: A wise son stores up in the summer, but a disgraceful son sleeps during harvest.
verses.6: Blessings crown the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked hides violence.
verses.7: The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
verses.8: A wise-hearted person accepts commandments, but a fool’s lips lead to ruin.
verses.9: One who walks with integrity walks with confidence, but the one who twists his ways will be known.
verses.10: One who winks with the eye sows discord, but a fool’s lips lead to ruin.
verses.11: A fountain of life is the mouth of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked hides violence.
verses.12: Hatred incites quarrels, but love covers all sins.
verses.13: Wisdom is found in the lips of the discerning, but a rod is for the back of the heartless.
verses.14: The wise guard knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is near ruin.
verses.15: The wealth of the rich is their city of strength, but the downfall of the wicked is their ruin.
verses.16: The fruit of the righteous is for life, but the fruit of the wicked is for sin.
verses.17: The path of life is for the one who keeps instruction, but the one who turns from correction strays.
verses.18: One who hides hatred with lying lips, and one who spreads gossip is a fool.
verses.19: In many words, there is no lack of wrongdoing, but one who holds back his lips is discerning.
verses.20: A refined silver tongue is the tongue of the righteous, but the heart of the wicked is worthless.
verses.21: The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools, heartless, will die.
verses.22: The blessing of the Lord enriches, and no sorrow will come with it.
verses.23: Doing evil is a joke to a fool, but wisdom is the delight of the discerning.
verses.24: The fear that the wicked have will come to them, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
verses.25: Like a storm that passes, the wicked will vanish, but the righteous will stand firm forever.
verses.26: Vinegar is bitter to the teeth and smoke is harsh to the eyes, so is the lazy to those who employ them.
verses.27: The fear of the Lord adds days, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.
verses.28: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectation of the wicked will perish.
verses.29: The path of the Lord is a stronghold for the innocent, but ruin for those who do evil.
verses.30: The righteous will not be shaken forever, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.
verses.31: The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom, but the tongue of the wicked is destroyed.
verses.32: The lips of the righteous know what pleases, but the mouth of the wicked is twisted.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son is the mother’s disgrace." — The Hebrew uses "יְשַׂמַּח־אָב" and "תוּגַת אִמּוֹ" to contrast the effect of the wise and foolish sons on their parents.
- v. 15: "The wealth of the rich is their city of strength" — The Hebrew metaphor "קִרְיַת עֻזּוֹ" is translated as "city of strength."
- v. 18: "One who hides hatred with lying lips" — The Hebrew uses "מְכַסֶּה שִׂנְאָה שִׂפְתֵי־שָׁקֶר" for the person who hides malice.
- v. 22: "The blessing of the Lord enriches, and no sorrow will come with it." — The Hebrew uses "תַּעֲשִׁיר" and "לֹֽא־יוֹסִיף עֶצֶב עִמָּֽהּ," indicating the blessing brings prosperity without grief.
